claims.claim_vi: A blocking algorithm uses locks; if thread A is suspended while holding the lock, thread B may wait for arbitrarily long and may starve.
claims.verified_by: Source body read from the pinned commit; the statement is in the source text.

claims.claim_vi: A non-blocking algorithm lets thread A access the queue but A must complete in a certain number of steps; thread B may still starve due to rejections.
claims.verified_by: Source body read from the pinned commit; the statement is in the source text.

claims.claim_vi: A blocking algorithm blocks B until the lock is released; a non-blocking algorithm notifies B that access is rejected.
claims.verified_by: Source body read from the pinned commit; the statement is in the source text.

claims.claim_vi: Starvation means a thread cannot acquire access to shared resources and cannot proceed; starvation-free means it does not occur; wait-free means all threads complete within a finite number of steps; wait-free = non-blocking + starvation-free.
claims.verified_by: Source body read from the pinned commit; the statement is in the source text.

claims.claim_vi: A non-blocking queue can be implemented with Compare and Swap (CAS).

claims.claim_vi: Benefits: no thread suspension (B gets a response immediately, lowering latency) and no deadlocks.
